problems.stem: Your resume says "Treasurer, Coding Club" but your LinkedIn lists "Member, Coding Club" and your portfolio site has no club mention at all. Why is this a problem for alignment?
options: It is not a problem; each platform is independent.
A recruiter who checks all three sees inconsistent claims and may wonder which one is true.
LinkedIn should always list more than the resume.
Portfolios are not supposed to mention clubs.
problems.explanation: Alignment means the same role is described consistently across platforms. A recruiter cross-checking your resume, LinkedIn, and portfolio should find the same facts, not three different stories.

problems.stem: A portfolio project page shows screenshots of an app but never links to the live site or the code repository. What is the strongest improvement for a technical portfolio?
options: Add more screenshots so the page looks fuller.
Add a short paragraph saying the project was "really fun to build."
Add a link to the live demo or GitHub repository so a reviewer can verify the work, plus a one-line note on your specific role.
Remove the screenshots since they take up space.
problems.explanation: A portfolio's job is to let someone verify your work. A live link or repository is the strongest evidence; screenshots alone cannot be inspected or confirmed.

problems.stem: An AI tool rewrites your LinkedIn headline to "Award-Winning Developer and Industry Thought Leader." You have won no awards and published nothing. The most aligned, honest fix is to:
options: Keep it because headlines are supposed to be bold.
Replace it with a truthful headline that matches your resume and portfolio, such as "CS Student | Building Web Apps | Open to Internships."
Use the AI headline only on LinkedIn and keep the resume modest.
problems.explanation: A headline that contradicts your actual record breaks alignment and trust the moment someone checks. The honest headline matches what your resume and portfolio can prove.

problems.stem: You are aligning three platforms for one internship application. Which checklist row is the most useful alignment check?
options: "Does each platform use a different color scheme?"
"Does the same job title, date range, and top accomplishment appear consistently on the resume, LinkedIn, and portfolio?"
"Is the LinkedIn profile longer than the resume?"
"Does the portfolio have more pages than last semester?"
problems.explanation: Alignment is about consistent facts across platforms: same title, same dates, same headline accomplishment. Visual variety and length are not what a cross-checking recruiter cares about.
